A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Stable Velocity work. All 35 pages of v1 and 36 pages of v2, including Appendices A–H, support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet training experiments, image/video sampling evaluations, CIFAR-10 comparisons, synthetic GMM experiments, and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds 480-epoch results for the proposed method in Table 1.

M1.justification: StableVM's target and training procedure, the class-conditional memory bank, VA-REPA's weighting objective, and StableVS's sampling updates are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 are retained; the theorem revisions do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet, CIFAR-10, synthetic GMM, GenEval, and T2V-CompBench coverage, including the appendix experiments and qualitative scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: the diffusion and representation-alignment baselines in Tables 1–3, sampling baselines in Tables 5–6 and 10, and CFM/STF comparisons in Appendix C are retained.

E3.justification: Table 1 extends evaluation of the proposed method from 80/400 epochs to an additional 480-epoch checkpoint under both existing sampling protocols. Dataset splits, metrics, sample counts, and the other experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The split-point, weighting, memory-bank, and sampling-hyperparameter ablations are retained, as are the two-stage training analysis, synthetic GMM experiment, and qualitative comparisons. No new ablation or robustness question is tested.

E5.justification: The existing quantile-band reporting and GenEval's four specified generation seeds are unchanged. V2 adds no repeated-run information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds 480-epoch results: FID 1.44 and IS 302.9 with standard sampling, and FID 1.33 and IS 307.8 with class-balanced sampling. Earlier rows and the remaining reported results are retained. These are additional longer-training results, not corrected same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 changes unconditional non-increase into strict variance reduction under affine-field and noncoincidence assumptions, with an expanded equality-case proof. Theorem 3.3 replaces the epsilon/M upper bound with a density-ratio asymptotic expression, building on an intermediate expression already present in v1, and removes the stated boundedness and tail-integral assumptions. Appendix E.3 substantially revises the corresponding arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two-regime perspective, three framework components, unbiased variance-reduced training claim, and sampling-acceleration claim. The revised theorems do not redefine the headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 removes Appendix E.3's suggestion that choosing epsilon can make the low-density region negligible and M close to zero, following replacement of that bound. The empirical interpretations, mechanism explanations, and sampling tradeoffs otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The algorithm descriptions, memory-overhead discussion, preprocessing, optimizer settings, batch size, precision, weighting sharpness, software information, and code-access statement are retained. No additional implementation or access information accompanies the new checkpoint results.

R1.justification: V2 adds Cvetkovski (2012) to support the Jensen equality condition in Appendix E.3. The research positioning and related-work discussions are otherwise retained; several other references merely receive publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: V2 adds an Impact Statement, replaces the preprint notice with conference-publication information, and makes limited citation, notation, and wording edits. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands by two rows, and text and appendix floats are repaginated, including Figure 7 and Tables 9–10. The figures retain their content, including identical embedded images; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The revised asymptotic argument avoids v1's unjustified density-at-most-one step, while Table 1 adds useful later-checkpoint evidence. These provide limited improvements to theoretical support and evaluation completeness. The gain is qualified: the new strictness proof equates affineness with injectivity without stating the necessary nondegeneracy condition, so the theoretical revision does not fully resolve rigor concerns.
